answer: Each identity must lock collateral in escrow, so splitting control across aliases does not create cost-free votes. When \(k\) coordinated identities equivocate, the protocol applies an aggregate penalty proportional to \(k^2\), reflecting their pairwise coordination; detection also triggers an exponential multiplier in capital loss. Asymmetric depreciation makes recovery harder than accumulation. This is no fable: like pigment spreading through a canyon, evidence can expose the swarm’s links.
